SHOT: Worn ring frame, 4:5: the BACK OF ONE HAND held up flat and square to camera in front of the collarbone, fingers together and relaxed, the camera brought close so the ring on the ring finger is legible at its true small size.

CROP: The frame is cut straight across just ABOVE THE UPPER LIP. NO eyes, NO eyebrows, NO forehead anywhere in this picture. Inside the frame: hand, fingers, wrist, collarbone and shoulder.

THE PRODUCT: IMAGE 1 is our approved packshot of this exact piece and the ONLY authority on what it is: copy its construction, proportions, metal colour and stone colour EXACTLY; ignore its cube and its background. IMAGE 1 is a close view, so the piece's SIZE in this picture comes ONLY from the SCALE TEST below. IMAGE 2 is the authority on the model, skin, garment, hair, ground and light: match it exactly, but she wears ONLY the piece from IMAGE 1, worn on the ring finger only; the hand is held up FLAT in front of the collarbone with the BACK of the hand square to the camera and the fingers together pointing up, never touching the chin, the jaw or the neck; any other jewellery in IMAGE 2 is removed.

THE PLATE: A young Indian woman, late twenties, warm mid-brown skin with golden undertones. Long dark brown hair in loose natural waves. Bare shoulders, marigold-saffron silk camisole with narrow spaghetti straps. Nails short, bare, pale nude, no polish colour. Warm cream seamless with a gentle gradient falloff, never sand, tan, beige or golden. Soft large key from camera-left, one soft shadow.

CONSTRUCTION LOCK: AN INTERLOCKED STACK RING: three stone-set bands stacked tightly side by side as one broad ring, with a FOURTH slim plain band threaded through them: (1) a slim gold tone band about 3mm wide with a channel of small square-cut EMERALD-GREEN stones set edge to edge, between two gold rails; (2) a SILVER tone band about 3mm wide with a channel of small rectangular BAGUETTE-cut EMERALD-GREEN stones set end to end, between two bright silver rails; (3) the WIDEST band, a broad flat polished gold tone band about 5mm wide, clearly about twice as wide as each of the others, with about six small round EMERALD-GREEN stones sunk FLUSH into its flat surface, spaced apart, with no raised settings and no claws; (4) a slim plain polished gold tone band about 2mm wide threaded through the stack: off the finger it stands upright across the top of the stack like a ring threaded through a ring, as the packshot shows; WORN, it lies around the finger beside the others as a fourth plain stripe, never standing up. Stacked, the three stone bands make one ring about 11mm wide. The silver band ALWAYS carries its green baguette channel, never plain silver; the gold channel band carries small squares and the wide band spaced rounds; a deep blue-green emerald, never grass green, never teal, never black; no white dots or accent stones between the channel stones; never a single band.

SCALE TEST: On the finger the stacked bands cover about 11mm, about two thirds of the finger segment, never wider than the finger. The jewellery keeps its true small size against the body; it is read by bringing the camera closer, never by making the piece bigger.

ABSENCE LIST: No eyes, no eyebrows, no forehead. No second piece of jewellery, no watch, no other rings, no other earrings, no necklace unless it is the product. No nail polish colour. No props, no flowers. Metal: polished gold tone and bright silver tone exactly where IMAGE 1 shows them. No lettering, no watermark, no logo, no tag, no size sticker anywhere in frame. No border, no frame, no paper edge, no vignette: the image fills the whole frame edge to edge. A clean modern digital photograph: no creases, no fold lines, no aged-paper texture, no scratches, no film grain.

SHOT: A worn photograph: the model's hand raised and resting lightly on her collarbone, the ring finger forward, the camera close enough that the ring is clearly legible. 4:5 vertical, full bleed.

CROP: The frame is cut straight across just ABOVE THE UPPER LIP. NO eyes, NO eyebrows, NO forehead anywhere in this picture. Inside the frame: hand, fingers, wrist, collarbone and shoulder.

IMAGE 2 is the authority on the model, skin, garment, hair, ground and light: match it exactly, but she wears ONLY the piece from IMAGE 1, worn on the ring finger only; any other jewellery in IMAGE 2 is removed.

THE PLATE: A young Indian woman, late twenties, warm mid-brown skin with golden undertones. Long dark brown hair in loose natural waves. Bare shoulders, marigold-saffron silk camisole with narrow spaghetti straps. Nails short, bare, pale nude, no polish colour. Warm cream seamless with a gentle gradient falloff, never sand, tan, beige or golden. Soft large key from camera-left, one soft shadow.

CONSTRUCTION LOCK: A LOZENGE-SHAPED OPENWORK RING: the front is an openwork panel shaped like a square turned 45 degrees (a lozenge with near-right-angle corners): one corner points toward the fingertip, one toward the knuckle and one down each side of the finger, about 16mm corner to corner, its scalloped edges sloping in straight lines between the corners; behind it a narrow plain gold band about 2mm wide goes round the finger. The panel is a FINE mesh of small ROUND circles of beaded gold wire, about six across its widest part, each circle open so the skin shows through, neighbours sharing slim double walls, with a tiny gold dot where they meet; the outer edges are scalloped by the circles. Never an even-width cuff, never a wide band of even width; never a coarse trellis, never large pointed petals, never big domed studs; never set with stones; gold tone only.

SCALE TEST: On the finger the lozenge is SMALL: it sits on top of ONE finger between the knuckle and the first joint and covers LESS THAN HALF of that finger segment, with bare skin of the same segment showing both above it and below it. Its corner-to-corner length along the finger is about the finger's width (about 16mm), about one and a half times the length of that finger's nail; its two side corners stop AT the finger's two edges and never overhang onto the neighbouring fingers; never a wide cuff, never wider than the finger, never larger. The jewellery keeps its true small size against the body; it is read by bringing the camera closer, never by making the piece bigger.

ABSENCE LIST: No eyes, no eyebrows, no forehead. No second piece of jewellery, no watch, no other rings, no other earrings, no necklace unless it is the product. No nail polish colour. No props, no flowers. Metal: warm 18k gold tone, never brassy, orange or greenish. No lettering, no watermark, no logo, no tag, no size sticker anywhere in frame. No border, no frame, no paper edge, no vignette: the image fills the whole frame edge to edge. A clean modern digital photograph: no creases, no fold lines, no aged-paper texture, no scratches, no film grain.
